name: Drunken Dockhand
narration: "A dockhand blocked the gangway," said Scheherazade, "three parts rum and one part fury."

name: Rat of the Hold
narration: "Something moved in the hold," said Scheherazade, "low and quick and unbothered by the dark."

name: Customs Officer
narration: "The customs officer demanded to see his papers," said Scheherazade, "and Sinbad, having none worth showing, drew his blade instead."

name: Pickpocket of the Souk
narration: "A hand slipped toward his belt in the crowded souk," said Scheherazade, "quick as a thought and twice as light-fingered."

name: Angry Pelican
narration: "A pelican, robbed of its catch by careless fishermen, decided the nearest sailor would do instead," said Scheherazade.

name: Pearl Diver
narration: "A pearl diver surfaced with empty hands and a temper to match," said Scheherazade, "and blamed the nearest stranger for her luck."

name: Ship's Cook
narration: "The ship's cook, furious that his galley had been raided, came swinging with the nearest thing still hot," said Scheherazade.

name: Sleepless Watchman
narration: "The watchman had not slept in three nights," said Scheherazade, "and mistook Sinbad for the ghost he'd been warned about."

name: Stray Ghul-pup
narration: "Astaghfirullah [I seek God's forgiveness]," whispered Scheherazade, "a small ghoul, orphaned from whatever bred it, snapped at his heels in the dark."

name: Snake Charmer's Serpent
narration: "The charmer's flute had stopped," said Scheherazade, "and the serpent, no longer charmed, remembered it was a serpent."

name: Superstitious Sailor
narration: "A sailor swore Sinbad's shadow fell wrong," said Scheherazade, "and drew steel against the evil eye he was certain he'd seen."

name: Cargo Mimic
narration: "Ya Allah [O God]," said Scheherazade, "the crate Sinbad reached for was not a crate at all."

name: The Whale That Was an Island
narration: "Mashallah [what God has willed]," breathed Scheherazade, "what they had thought an island rose from the sea, and the island had teeth."

name: The Bazaar
narration: "There was in that city a bazaar," said Scheherazade, "where anything could be bought — for the right story."

name: The Calligrapher
narration: "In a narrow stall sat the Calligrapher," said Scheherazade, "who for a price would re-ink a blade's story in gold leaf, and strengthen it in the telling."

name: The House of Forgetting
narration: "Behind a curtained doorway was a tavern thick with lotus-smoke," said Scheherazade, "where a man might trade a memory for silence — for wallahi [I swear by God], some verses are best left untold."

name: The Jinni of the Lamp
narration: "Half-buried in the sand, a brass lamp caught the light," said Scheherazade, "and from its spout curled a Jinni, already bargaining."

name: The Bashful Oyster
narration: "An oyster lay half-buried in the sand," said Scheherazade, "clamped shut like a secret too shy to tell — though a pearl gleamed within, for those with patient hands."

name: The Greedy Jar
narration: "A sealed jar sat too neatly on the dock," said Scheherazade, "and something inside it wanted, very badly, to be opened."

name: Turn the Page
narration: "Scheherazade turned the page," she said, "and where the ink had been blank, a new scene bloomed to take its place."
